title: Invertible counit transports a perfect pairing to pushforward
statement: Let p:X→Y be a scheme map [def-pc-scheme], with tensor-pullback adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] whose unit at O_Y is invertible. For M,D on X and ev:M⊗D→O_X with invertible curry, suppose the counit at M is invertible. Then the curry of the explicit pushed-forward pairing [def-sc-picard-cup-product-map] is invertible. No local freeness of p_*M is assumed.

source.place: final paragraph, perfect pairing and the two displayed mutually dual bases

proof.text: For every Y-module P identify Hom(P,p_*D) with Hom(p^*P,D) by adjunction, then with Hom(M⊗p^*P,O_X) by the perfect evaluation. Use the invertible counit to replace M by p^*p_*M.

Use the tensor comparison to identify the tensor source with p^*(p_*M⊗P). Identify O_X with p^*O_Y, apply adjunction and the inverse structure-sheaf unit, then curry. This produces a bijection Hom(P,p_*D)≃Hom(P,dual(p_*M)).

Naturality of the tensor comparison in its second factor follows from naturality of its inverse monoidal comparison. Together with adjunction naturality and the proved cup counit identity, it identifies the bijection with postcomposition by the cup transpose. The Yoneda criterion isIso_iff_yoneda_map_bijective proves invertibility. This argument includes zero modules and empty schemes.
